holding_summary: The court affirmed a judgment finding that a mother's sale of property to her daughter was actually a donation in disguise because the daughter failed to prove payment of a fourth of the property's value, and that a son long recognized by his siblings as their brother was presumed legitimate, a presumption not overcome by the evidence. The eviction suit against the brother therefore failed, and the property was ordered collated and partitioned among all heirs.

quotes.text: The daughter, Josephine, before and after her marriage, worked as a laundress and had boarders and lodgers, for whom she did the cooking. One of the boarders slept in the shack where Richard Kelly lived, and five of them slept in the house occupied by the mother and daughter.
We concur in the opinion of the district judge that the plaintiff failed to prove that she had paid her mother as much as a fourth of the value of the property.

notes: Boarding/lodging by the daughter (and use of a room by a boarder in the shack where the eventual eviction defendant lived) appears only as unadjudicated background fact explaining the family's income; the court never characterizes the arrangement's legal nature, so characterization is left null. Main holding concerns donation-in-disguise and legitimacy presumption, unrelated to lodging law.

Zoning case about denial of a moving-picture-theater building permit; boarding houses, apartment houses, and hotels are mentioned only as an exempted category in the zoning ordinance's list of permitted uses, never litigated or characterized by the court. Relator was held to lack standing to even raise the exemption. Passing mention only.
Separation-from-bed-and-board suit over husband's right to select the matrimonial domicile with his parents; no compensated letting of rooms or a dwelling is at issue.
Concerns a municipal ordinance banning paid-admission public dances as a nuisance under the police power; no lodging or boarding house issue present.
Succession/partition dispute over family-meeting procedural formalities preceding a private sale of minors' inherited land; no lodging or boarding issue.
Zoning-ordinance validity challenge concerning denial of a permit for a private meat market; no lodging or boarding house issue.

Commercial lease of a restaurant premises; dispute over lessor's duty to maintain the leased building during wall reconstruction. Ordinary commercial landlord-tenant law, not residential lodging or boarding.
Zoning dispute over whether a formerly-vacant commercial building retained its business classification when reused as a real-estate office and tearoom/restaurant. No lodging or boarding issue.

Port authority's power to sell surplus land and dispute over mortgage coverage; a prior case's lease of a warehouse to a private corporation is discussed only as precedent for the board's incidental powers, unrelated to residential lodging or boarding.
Commercial retail-store lease breach and damages dispute, including a call in warranty against a prior commercial tenant; no residential lodging or boarding issue.
Boundary and mortgage-description dispute over a plantation tract sold per aversionem; no lodging or boarding issue.
Municipal ordinance prohibiting liquor sales, upheld under the police power; no lodging or boarding house issue.
Venue/jurisdiction dispute over the husband's matrimonial domicile in a separation suit; discusses the spouses' 'common dwelling' but involves no compensated letting of rooms to third parties.
Dispute over the vested-rights effect of a building permit for a filling station following zoning ordinance changes; no lodging or boarding issue.
Zoning/nuisance dispute over removal of gasoline filling stations and pumps from a street; no lodging or boarding house issue.
Commercial lease dispute over a shared alleyway entrance/exit used for washing automobiles, and a resulting rent-reduction claim; no residential lodging issue.
Natural-drainage servitude dispute between an irrigation canal and an adjoining public road; no lodging or boarding issue.
Commercial lease of an auto-garage business premises and liability of a successor occupant for rent; no residential lodging or boarding issue.
